title: Remark
body_md:
We note that our new construction of exact locally dense lattices implies new hardness results for $\mathrm{SVP}_p$, using the techniques in~\cite{AS18}. (We do not attempt to prove these hardness results formally, as this is not the focus of the present work.) Specifically our construction of exact locally dense lattices with exponential $N$ for $p > 2$ (in \cref{cor: alpha to kissing number}, which is the key step in proving \cref{item:main_theorem_exp} of \cref{thm:kn-lower-bounds-main}) implies (randomized) SETH-hardness of $\mathrm{SVP}_p$ for all $p > 2$, rather than just for $p > p_0 \approx 2.1397$. It also implies slightly improved SETH-hardness for $p_0 < p < p_1 \approx 2.1433$, since our construction achieves larger $N$ than the construction in \cite{AS18} for such $p$. (Here $p_0$ and $p_1$ are the values of $p$ described above; see \cref{fig:high_p_plot}.)

Additionally, we note that the (randomized) construction in \cref{thm:craig} of $(p, n, N)$-\emph{exact} locally dense lattices for any $p$ (including $p = 2$) and $N \geq 2^{\Omega(\sqrt{n})}$ implies $2^{\Omega(\sqrt{n})}$-hardness of $\mathrm{SVP}_p$ under \emph{non-gap} randomized ETH. This construction was essentially already present in \cite{conf/random/BennettP23} and even earlier work may yield constructions of (potentially non-exact) locally dense lattices with similar parameters (which would lead to hardness under a gap version of ETH). To the best of our knowledge, no prior work has shown such hardness for $\mathrm{SVP}_2$.

title: Proof

     \|\bm{v}-z\bm{t}\|_p\ge \operatorname{dist}_p(z\bm{t},\mathcal{L})\ge \operatorname{dist}_p(\bm{t},\mathcal{L}).

label: thm:ball_point_count
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:ball_point_count}
For any lattice $\mathcal{L}\subseteq \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^n$, any radius $r>0$, and any $\tau > 0$,
\[
    N_p(\mathcal{L},r) < \min_{\tau >0} e^{\tau r^p}\Theta_p(\mathcal{L},\tau)
    \; .
\]
In particular, $N_p(\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}^n,n^{1/p}/2) < c_p^n$ where
\[
c_p:=\min_{\tau>0}e^{\tau/2^{p}}\sum_{z\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}}e^{-\tau|z|^{p}}
\; .
\]
Furthermore, when $p > p_0 $, then $0<c_p < 2$, where
 $p_0 \approx 2.1397$ is defined as the unique value such that $c_{p_0} = 2$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We use the following observation in~\cite{AS18}. For $r>0$, $\Theta_p(\mathcal{L},\tau)> \sum_{\bm{y}\in \mathcal{L},\|\bm{y}\|_p\le r}e^{-\tau\|\bm{y}\|_p^p}\ge N_p(\mathcal{L},r) e^{-\tau r^p}$, and hence $N_p(\mathcal{L},r)<e^{\tau r^p}\Theta_p(\mathcal{L},\tau)$. Taking the minimum over $\tau>0$ (it is easy to see that the minimum is achieved), we get
\[
    N_p(\mathcal{L},r)< \min_{\tau>0} e^{\tau r^p}\Theta_p(\mathcal{L},\tau)\ .
\]
For $\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}^n$, we also have that
\begin{align}
\Theta_p(\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}^n,\tau)=\sum_{\bm{z}\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}^n}e^{-\tau\|\bm{z}\|_p^p}&=\sum_{z_1,\dots,z_n\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}}e^{-\tau\sum_{i=1}^n|z_i|^p}\notag\\
 
&= \left(\sum_{z\in \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}}e^{-\tau |z|^p}\right)^n\notag\\
&=\Theta_p(\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}},\tau)^n. \label{eq:orthogonal-to-power-theta}
\end{align}
This implies $N_p(\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}^n,r)< \left(\min_{\tau>0} e^{\tau r^p/n}\Theta_p(\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}},\tau) \right)^n$.

Fix $r=n^{1/p}/2$. Let $g(p,\tau)=e^{\tau/2^{p}}\sum_{z\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}}e^{-\tau|z|^{p}}$, where $p\ge 1,\tau>0$. Let $c_p:=\min_{\tau>0}g(p,\tau)$, we have
\[
N_p(\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}^n,\frac12 n^{1/p})< \left(\min_{\tau>0} e^{\tau /2^p}\Theta_p(\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}},\tau) \right)^n=\left(\min_{\tau>0}g(p,\tau)\right)^n=c_p^n.
\]
Since $|z|=0$ or $|z|\ge 1$, for a fixed $\tau$, $g(p,\tau)$ is strictly decreasing with $p$. $\min_{\tau>0}g(p,\tau)=2$ is achieved at $p_0\approx 2.1397$ (which can be easily computed to high accuracy, as is discussed in \cite{AS18}), and monotonicity shows that $p_0$ is unique. This proves that for any $p>p_0$, $c_p=\min_{\tau>0}g(p,\tau)<\min_{\tau>0}g(p_0,\tau)=2$.

label: lem:sparsification-25
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{lem:sparsification-25}
    Let $p\ge 1$, $n\ge 2$, $\mathcal{L}$ be a lattice of rank $n$ with basis $\ensuremath{\bm{B}}$, $\bm{t}\in\operatorname{span}(\mathcal{L})\setminus \mathcal{L}$. For $r>0$, let $$A=|\{\bm{y}-k\bm{t}:\bm{y}\in\mathcal{L},k\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}},\|\bm{y}-k\bm{t}\|_p<r\}|<\infty,\quad G=|\{\bm{v}\in \mathcal{L}:\|\bm{v}-\bm{t}\|_p=r\}|.$$ Let $q>A$ be an odd prime, $s=\min\{z\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}_{\ge 1}:z\bm{t}\in\mathcal{L}\}$, and $\bm{d}\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}^n$ be such that $\ensuremath{\bm{B}}\bm{d} = s\bm{t}$. 

    
    
    Assume $q\nmid s$, sample $\bm{a}$ uniformly over $\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}^n_q$ and fix $\bm{z} = s^*\bm{d}$ where $s^*$ is any representative of $s^{-1}\pmod q$ in $\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}$. Define 
    \[
    \mathcal{L}' = \{\ensuremath{\bm{B}} \bm{x}:\bm{x}\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}^n,\langle \bm{x},\bm{a}\rangle\equiv 0\pmod q\},\quad \bm{t}':=\bm{t}-\ensuremath{\bm{B}}\bm{z}.
    \]
    Then $\mathcal{L}'$ has rank $n$, $\mathcal{L}'+\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}\bm{t}'$ is a lattice, and the following hold:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item \label{item-one-BPT25}(Minimum distance.) $
\Pr[\lambda_1^{(p)}(\mathcal{L}'+\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}\bm{t}')<r]\le \frac{A-1}{q}$.
        \item \label{item-two-BPT25} (Close vector count.) For any $\delta>0$, $\Pr[N_p(\mathcal{L}'-\bm{t}',r)\le (1-\delta)\cdot\frac{G}{q}]\le\frac{Cq}{\delta^2 G}$, where $C=1$ if $s> 2$, and $C=2$ if $s=2$.
    \end{enumerate}

title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:kannans-embedding-formal}
Fix any $p\ge 1$, let $(\mathcal{L}, \bm{t})$ be a $(p, n, N)$-exact locally dense lattice. Then $\mathcal{L}+\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}\bm{t}$ is a lattice with $\kappa_p(\mathcal{L}+\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}\bm{t}) \ge N$.
head: environment
name: Kissing number from exact locally dense lattice

title: Proof
body_md: \cref{lem:well-definedness of lattice} shows that $\mathcal{L}+\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}\bm{t}$ is a lattice; in particular, it is discrete. For every $\bm{w} =\bm{v}+z\bm{t}$ for $\bm{v}\in\mathcal{L},z\in \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}$, if $z\bm{t}\in\mathcal{L}$ then $\bm{w}\in\mathcal{L}$ and $\|\bm{w}\|_p\ge\lambda_1^{(p)}(\mathcal{L})\ge\operatorname{dist}_p(\bm{t},\mathcal{L})$ (unless $\bm{w}=\bm{0}$). Otherwise, $\|\bm{w}\|_p\ge\operatorname{dist}_p(-z\bm{t},\mathcal{L})=\operatorname{dist}_p(|z|\bm{t},\mathcal{L})\ge\operatorname{dist}_p(\bm{t},\mathcal{L})$. Since $\operatorname{dist}_p(\bm{t},\mathcal{L})$ is achieved by vectors in $\operatorname{CVP}_p(\bm{t},\mathcal{L})-\bm{t}$, which has size at least $N$, this proves $\lambda_1^{(p)}(\mathcal{L}+\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}\bm{t}) = \operatorname{dist}_p(\bm{t},\mathcal{L})$ and $\kappa_p(\mathcal{L}+\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}\bm{t}) \geq N$.

label: thm:sparsification
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:sparsification} 
Fix any $p\ge 1$. For all sufficiently large $n$, let $\mathcal{L}\subseteq \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^m$ be a rank $n$ lattice, and $\bm{t}\in\mathrm{span}(\mathcal{L})\setminus\mathcal{L}$ be a target vector.  For $r>0$, define $A = A(\mathcal{L},\bm{t},r)$ and $G = G(\mathcal{L},\bm{t},r)$ as
$$A :=|\{ \bm{y}-k\bm{t} :\bm{y}\in\mathcal{L}, k \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}, \|\bm{y} - k \bm{t}\|_p < r\}|<\infty,\quad G :=|\{\bm{x}\in\mathcal{L}:\|\bm{x}-\bm{t}\|_p=r\}| \ \text{.}$$
If $G/A\ge 64$, then there exists a rank $n$ sublattice $\mathcal{L}'\subseteq\mathcal{L}$ and target $\bm{t}'$ that form a $(p,n,G/(8A))$-exact locally dense lattice. In particular, $\kappa_p(\mathcal{L}'+\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}\bm{t}') \geq G/(8A)$ by \cref{thm:kannans-embedding-formal}.
head: environment
name: Exact locally dense lattice from sparsification

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $q$ be a prime in the range $(2A,4A)$.
 
Such a prime is guaranteed to exist by Bertrand's postulate.

We apply the sparsification result in~\cref{lem:sparsification-25} to obtain the sublattice $\mathcal{L}'\subseteq\mathcal{L}$ and target $\bm{t}'$. In particular, we have that $\mathcal{L}'+\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}\bm{t}'$ is a lattice. More interestingly,
\[
\Pr[\lambda_1^{(p)}(\mathcal{L}'+\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}\bm{t}')<r]\le \frac{A-1}{q}
\]
and
\[\Pr\Big[N_p(\mathcal{L}'-\bm{t}',r)\le \frac{G}{2q} \Big]<\frac{8q}{G}
\; ,
\]
where we take $\delta=\frac12$ in~\cref{item-two-BPT25} of \cref{lem:sparsification-25}. This then implies that with probability at least $1-\frac{A-1}{q}-\frac{8q}{G}>\frac12-\frac{32A}{G}\ge 0$, all of the following hold:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item $\operatorname{dist}_p(\bm{t}',\mathcal{L}')=r\le \lambda_1^{(p)}(\mathcal{L}')$.
    \item $|\operatorname{CVP}_p(\bm{t}',\mathcal{L}')|\ge \frac{G}{2q}>\frac{G}{8A}$.
    \item For integer $k$, either $k\bm{t}'\in\mathcal{L}'$ or $\operatorname{dist}_p(\bm{t}',\mathcal{L}')=r\le \operatorname{dist}_p(k\bm{t}',\mathcal{L}')$.
\end{enumerate}
In other words, with non-zero probability, $\mathcal{L}'$ and $\bm{t}'$ form a $(p,n,G/(8A))$-exact locally dense lattice.

label: thm:craig
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:craig}
For any prime $q \geq 5$, there exists a target $\bm{t}\in\{0,1\}^q$ such that $(A_{q-1}^{(m)},\bm{t})$ is $(p,q-1,\Omega(e^{\sqrt q}q^{3/4}))$-exact locally dense for all $p \geq 1$ with $m :=  \lfloor\sqrt{q}/2\rfloor$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Consider the lattice $A_{q-1}^{(m)}$, note $1\le m=\lfloor\frac{\sqrt q}{2}\rfloor\le\frac{q}2$. For any vector $\bm{s}\in\{0,1\}^q$ define $f:\{0,1\}^q\to \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}_q^{m-1}$ as  

\[
f(\bm{s}) = \left(\sum_{i=1}^q s_i\cdot i^j \bmod q\right)_{1\le j<m}.
\] 

Recalling the definition of the Craig lattice $A_{q-1}^{(m)}$ from \cref{def:craig}, we see that for any $\bm{s}, \bm{t} \in \{0,1\}^q$, we have that $\bm{t} - \bm{s} \in A_{q-1}^{(m)}$ if (and only if) $\|\bm{s}\|_1 = \|\bm{t}\|_1$ and $f(\bm{s}) = f(\bm{t})$.
Since all coordinates of $f(\bm{s})$ are in $\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}_q$, we see that there are at most $q^{m-1}$ values for $f(\bm{s})$. It follows from the pigeonhole principle that there must be some fixed value of $f(\bm{s})$ that is achieved by at least
\[\frac{\binom{q}{2m}}{q^{m-1}}
\]
distinct choices of $\bm{s} \in \{0,1\}^q$ with $\|\bm{s}\|_1 = 2m$. Using~\cref{fact:binom} and that $\sqrt q-2<2m\le \sqrt q$, we have 
\[
\binom{q}{2m}\geq \Omega\left(q^{m-\frac14}e^{2m}\right).
\]
Hence 
\[
\frac{\binom{q}{2m}}{q^{m-1}}\geq \Omega\left(\frac{q^{m-\frac14}e^{2m}}{q^{m-1}}\right)\geq\Omega(e^{\sqrt q}q^{3/4}).
\]
Let $\bm{t} \in \set{0, 1}^q$ be such that $f(\bm{s}) = f(\bm{t})$ and $\|\bm{s}\|_1 = \|\bm{t}\|_1$ for at least $\binom{q}{2m}/q^{m-1}$ elements $\bm{s} \in \set{0, 1}^q$.
Then for such $\bm{t}$ and $\bm{s}$, we have $\|(\bm{t}- \bm{s}) - \bm{t}\|_p = \|\bm{s}\|_p= (2m)^{1/p}$, so that there are at least $N$ lattice vectors with distance exactly $(2m)^{1/p}$ from $\bm{t}$.

To show that this is an exact locally dense lattice, it therefore suffices to show that $\lambda_1^{(p)}(A_{q-1}^{(m)}) \geq (2m)^{1/p}$ and that $\operatorname{dist}_p( k\bm{t},A_{q-1}^{(m)}) \geq (2m)^{1/p}$ for all $k \geq 1$. In fact, the lower bound on $\lambda_1^{(p)}(A_{q-1}^{(m)})$ is exactly \cref{thm:minimum bound}. To show that $\operatorname{dist}_p( k\bm{t},A_{q-1}^{(m)}) \geq (2m)^{1/p}$, let $\bm{v} \in A_{q-1}^{(m)}$ and consider $\bm{w} := \bm{v} - k\bm{t} \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}^q$. Note that $\sum_{i=1}^q v_i = 0$ by the definition of $A_{q-1}^{(m)}$, so that 
\[
\|\bm{w}\|_p^p\ge\|\bm{w}\|_1\ge\bigg|\sum_{i=1}^qw_i\bigg| = \bigg|\sum_{i=1}^qv_i-k(2m)\bigg|=k(2m)\ge 2m
\; ,
\]
as needed.

title: Proof
body_md:
Recall $A_{q-1}^{(k)}=\mathcal{L}_{q,k}\cap\{\bm{x}\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^q:\sum_{i=1}^q x_i=0\}$. For any vector $\bm{u}\in S_2(\bm{y},2k)$, we see that $\bm{u}-\bm{y}\in\mathcal{L}_{q,k}$. Notice $\sum_{i=1}^q(\bm{u}-\bm{y})_i=0$ as $\bm{u},\bm{y}$ are boolean vectors with equal Hamming weight. This implies $\pm(S_2(\bm{y},2k)-\bm{y})\subseteq A_{q-1}^{(k)}$. 

    Let $\bm{v}:=\bm{w}-z\bm{y}$ for some $\bm{w}\in A_{q-1}^{(k)}$ and integer $z\ge 1$. Since $\sum_{i=1}^qw_i =  0 $ by the definition, we see that
    \[
    \sum_{i=1}^qv_i= -z\sum_{i=1}^qy_i= -2zk,
    \]
    since $\bm{y}$ has Hamming weight $2k$. Therefore $\|\bm{v}\|_p^p\ge\left|\sum_{i=1}^qv_i\right|= 2zk$, where we use the fact that $\bm{v}\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}^q$. For $z=1$ this shows $\operatorname{dist}_p(\bm{y},A_{q-1}^{(k)})\ge(2k)^{1/p}$, with equality obtained by vectors in $\bm{y}-S_2(\bm{y},2k)$. For $z\ge 2$, this proves $\operatorname{dist}_p(z\bm{y},A_{q-1}^{(k)})\ge\operatorname{dist}_p(\bm{y},A_{q-1}^{(k)})$. Since~\cref{thm:minimum bound} shows $\lambda_1^{(p)}(A_{q-1}^{(k)})\ge (2k)^{1/p}$, \cref{cor:refinement of wan} implies $(A_{q-1}^{(k)},\bm{y})$ is a $(p,q-1,2^{\Omega(q^{1/4}\log q)})$-exact locally dense lattice, as needed.

label: lem:closestvectorcount
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:closestvectorcount}
For $p>2$, let $\bm{t}=H_m\bm{e}_1,\mathcal{M}_m=H_mD_m$, we have $|\operatorname{CVP}_p(\bm{t},\mathcal{M}_m)|=2m$, and $\operatorname{dist}_p(\bm{t},\mathcal{M}_m)=m^{1/p}$.
head: environment
name: Closest vectors are preserved by Hadamard

title: Proof
body_md:
Recall $\operatorname{CVP}_p(\bm{e}_1,D_m)=\{\bm{e}_1\pm\bm{e}_i:1\le i\le m\}$. After applying $H_m$, for $\bm{u}\in \operatorname{CVP}_p(\bm{e}_1,D_m)$, $\|H_m\bm{u}-\bm{t}\|_p=\|H_m\bm{u}-H_m\bm{e}_1\|_p=m^{1/p}$ by~\cref{fact: Hadamard}, since $\bm{u}-\bm{e}_1\in\{\pm\bm{e}_i:1\le i\le m\}$. Therefore, the vectors in $H_m\operatorname{CVP}_p(\bm{e}_1,D_m)$ are at distance $m^{1/p}$ to $\bm{t}$, and they are clearly distinct.

It remains to show that these are the closest vectors. For any $\bm{w}\notin H_m\operatorname{CVP}_p(\bm{e}_1,D_m)$, let $\bm{w}=H_m\bm{z}$ for some $\bm{z}\in D_m$. Then $\bm{z}$ is not a closest vector to $\bm{e}_1$ in $D_m$, hence $\|\bm{z}-\bm{e}_1\|_2> 1$. This implies 
\[
\|\bm{w}-\bm{t}\|_p=\|H_m(\bm{z}-\bm{e}_1)\|_p\ge m^{1/p}\|\bm{z}-\bm{e}_1\|_2>m^{1/p}\ ,
\]
where the first inequality results from~\cref{lem:Hamadard norm}.
This proves $\operatorname{CVP}_p(\bm{t},\mathcal{M}_m)=H_m\operatorname{CVP}_p(\bm{e}_1,D_m)$, so $|\operatorname{CVP}_p(\bm{t},\mathcal{M}_m)|=2m$, and $\operatorname{dist}_p(\bm{t},\mathcal{M}_m)=m^{1/p}$.

label: thm: general G and A
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
\cref{lem:closestvectorcount} shows $\operatorname{dist}_p(\bm{t},\mathcal{M}_m)=m^{1/p}$ and $|\operatorname{CVP}_p(\bm{t},\mathcal{M}_m)|=2m$, therefore $\operatorname{dist}_p(\bm{t}^\ell,\mathcal{M}_m^\ell)=(m\ell)^{1/p}$ and $|\operatorname{CVP}_p(\bm{t}^\ell,\mathcal{M}_m^\ell)|=(2m)^{\ell}$ (since $\operatorname{CVP}_p(\bm{t}^\ell,\mathcal{M}_m^\ell)=\operatorname{CVP}_p^{\oplus \ell}(\bm{t},\mathcal{M}_m)$). So $$G(\mathcal{M}_m^\ell,\bm{t}^\ell,(m\ell)^{1/p})=(2m)^{\ell}.$$ 
    Since $\bm{t}^\ell\notin\mathcal{M}_m^\ell$ and $2\bm{t}^\ell\in\mathcal{M}_m^\ell$, $\{ \bm{y} - k\bm{t}^\ell\ : k \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}},\ \bm{y} \in \mathcal{M}_m^\ell\}$ is the union of $\{ \bm{y} - k\bm{t}^\ell\ : k \in 2\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}},\ \bm{y} \in \mathcal{M}_m^\ell\} = \mathcal{M}_m^\ell $ and $\{\bm{y} - k\bm{t}^\ell \ : \ k \in 2\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}} +1, \bm{y} \in \mathcal{M}_m^\ell \} = \mathcal{M}_m^\ell + \bm{t}^\ell$. Note the second set contributes no vector shorter than $(m\ell)^{1/p}$. Using~\cref{eq:orthogonal_theta_bound}, we get $1\le A(\mathcal{M}_m^\ell,\bm{t}^\ell,(m\ell)^{1/p})\le \min_{\tau>0} \, e^{\tau m\ell} \cdot \Theta_p(\mathcal{M}_m,\tau)^{\ell}$. Hence the result follows.

label: cor: alpha to kissing number
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor: alpha to kissing number}
    Fix any $p>2$, constant $k\ge 0$, and $m=2^k$. Define
    \[
    \alpha_{p,m} :=\left(\frac{2m}{\min_{\tau>0} \, e^{\tau m} \cdot \Theta_p(\mathcal{M}_m,\tau)}\right)^{1/m} \ \text{.}
    \]
    For $\ell>0$ and $n:=m\ell$, there exists a full-rank sublattice $\mathcal{M}'\subseteq \mathcal{M}_m^\ell$ and target $\bm{t}'$, such that $(\mathcal{M}',\bm{t}')$ is $(p,n,\Omega(\alpha_{p,m}^{n}))$-exact locally dense. In particular, $\kappa_p(\mathcal{M}'+\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}\bm{t}')\ge \Omega(\alpha_{p,m}^{n})$.

    Therefore, for all $n$, $\kappa_p(n) \geq \Omega(\alpha_{p,m}^{n})$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The statement is vacuous when $\alpha_{p,m} \leq 1$, so we may assume $\alpha_{p,m} > 1$.

For $\mathcal{M}_m^\ell,\bm{t}^\ell$ and radius $(m\ell)^{1/p}$, we have $G/A\ge \alpha_{p,m}^{m\ell}=\alpha^n_{p,m}$ by~\cref{thm: general G and A}. When $\alpha_{p,m}>1$, for sufficiently large $\ell$, this gives $G/A\ge 64$. So, we can apply \cref{thm:sparsification}, which implies the existence of the sublattice $\mathcal{M}'\subseteq \mathcal{M}_m^\ell$ and $\bm{t}'$ such that $(\mathcal{M}',\bm{t}')$ is $(p,n,\Omega(\alpha_{p,m}^{n}))$-exact locally dense, and that $\kappa_p(\mathcal{M}'+\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}\bm{t}')\ge \Omega(\alpha_{p,m}^{n})$.

This implies that $\kappa_p(n) \geq \Omega(\alpha_{p,m}^n)$ for $n$ divisible by $m$. A simple padding argument similar to~\cref{rmk:padding} then shows the result for all $n$.

label: lem: directsumshortbound
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem: directsumshortbound}
For any $p > 2$ and $\tau>0$,
\[
\Theta_p(\mathcal{M}_m,\tau)\le\Theta_2(\mathcal{M}_m,\tau/\mu)=\Theta_2(D_m,\tau m/\mu)
\; ,
\]
where $\mu := 2^{1 - p/2} < 1$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For all $\bm{v}\in D_m$, if $\bm{v}\ne \bm{0}$, then $\|\bm{v}\|_2\ge \sqrt{2}$, so $\|H_m\bm{v}\|_2\ge \sqrt {2m}$.
Therefore, \cref{fact: norm conversion} gives
\[
\|H_m\bm{v}\|_p^p\ge (m^{1/p-1/2}\|H_m\bm{v}\|_2)^p=m^{1-p/2} \|H_m \bm{v}\|_2^{p-2} \|H_m\bm{v}\|_2^2\ge m^{1-p/2}(\sqrt{2m})^{p-2}\|H_m\bm{v}\|_2^2=\|H_m\bm{v}\|_2^2/\mu.
\]
From this, it follows that
\[
\Theta_p(\mathcal{M}_m,\tau)=\sum_{\bm{v}\in D_m}e^{-\tau \|H_m\bm{v}\|_p^p}\le \sum_{\bm{v}\in D_m}e^{-\tau \|H_m\bm{v}\|_2^2/\mu}=\Theta_2(\mathcal{M}_m,\tau /\mu).
\]
Finally, the equality follows from the fact that $H_m$ is a scaled rotation. In particular,
\[
\Theta_2(\mathcal{M}_m,\tau/\mu)=\sum_{\bm{v}\in D_m}e^{-\tau \|H_m\bm{v}\|_2^2/\mu}=\sum_{\bm{v}\in D_m}e^{-\tau m \|\bm{v}\|_2^2/\mu}=\Theta_2(D_m,\tau m/\mu). \qedhere
\]
head: environment

label: lem:chosen tau bound
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
\cref{lem: directsumshortbound} gives $\Theta_p(\mathcal{M}_m,\tau)\le \Theta_2(D_m,\tau m/\mu)$, and we trivially have  that $\Theta_2(D_m,\tau m/\mu)\le \Theta_2(\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}^m,\tau m/\mu)$.
Let $\tau :=\mu\ln(m)/m$. Then,
\[
\Theta_p(\mathcal{M}_m,\tau)\le \sum_{\bm{v}\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}^m}e^{-\tau m\|\bm{v}\|_2^2/\mu}\le \sum_{\bm{v}\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}^m}m^{-\|\bm{v}\|_2^2}=\left(\sum_{z\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}}m^{-z^2}\right)^m \ \text{,}
\]
and
\[
\sum_{z\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}}m^{-z^2}=1+2\sum_{z\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}_{>0}}m^{-z^2}\le 1+2\sum_{z\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}_{>0}}m^{-z}=1+\frac{2m^{-1}}{1-m^{-1}}=1+\frac{2}{m-1} \ \text{.}
\]
 

Differentiation shows that $\left(1+\frac{2}{m-1}\right)^m$ is strictly decreasing for $m\ge 2$, and so
\[
\Theta_p(\mathcal{M}_m,\tau)\le \left(1+\frac{2}{m-1}\right)^m \leq \left(1+\frac{2}{2-1}\right)^2 = 9 \ \text{.}
\]
We have that $e^{\tau m}=m^{\mu}$, and so this gives
\[
\alpha_{p,m}^m\ge\frac{2m}{9\cdot m^\mu}=\frac{2m^{1-\mu}}{9} \ \text{,}
\]
as needed.

title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{thm:last-one}
For any constant $p > 2$,

head: environment
name: Exponential kissing number for $p>2$

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\mu := 2^{1-p/2} < 1$.
Let $\widehat{m} := e (9/2)^{1/(1-\mu)}$. A quick check shows that the function $f_p(m) := (2m^{1-\mu}/9)^{1/m}$ arising in \cref{lem:chosen tau bound} is decreasing for $m > \widehat{m}$. So, let $m$ be the first power of two larger than $\widehat{m}$, so that in particular $f_p(m) \geq f_p(2\widehat{m})$. It follows from \cref{lem:chosen tau bound} that
\[
    \alpha_p \geq \alpha_{p,m} \geq f_p(m) \geq f_p(2\widehat{m}) = (2e)^{(1-\mu)/(2 \widehat{m})} > 1
    \; ,
\]
and the result follows from \cref{cor: alpha to kissing number}.

label: lem:order-of-t
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:order-of-t}
    Let $p\ge 1$, $\mathcal{L}$ be a lattice of rank $n$ with basis $\ensuremath{\bm{B}}$, $\bm{t}\in\operatorname{span}(\mathcal{L})$, and $r > 0$. Let 
    \[A:=|\{\bm{y}-k\bm{t}:\bm{y}\in\mathcal{L},k\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}},\|\bm{y}-k\bm{t}\|_p<r\}|
    \; .
    \]
    If $A$ is finite, then there exists an integer $z>0$, such that $z\bm{t}\in\mathcal{L}$. Furthermore, $\mathcal{L}+\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}\bm{t}$ is a lattice.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\mathcal{L}=\mathcal{L}(\ensuremath{\bm{B}})$, $S=[0,1)^n\subseteq \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^n$, define $\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{L}):=\ensuremath{\bm{B}} S$. For any $\bm{x}\in \mathrm{span}(\mathcal{L})$, it is easy to see that there exist unique $\bm{v}\in\mathcal{L},\bm{p}\in\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{L})$, such that $\bm{x}=\bm{v}+\bm{p}$. We write $\bm{p}=\bm{x}\mod \mathcal{L}$. 

Now, if for all integer $z\ge 1$ we have $z\bm{t}\notin\mathcal{L}$, let $Z:=\{z\bm{t}\mod\mathcal{L}:z\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}_{\ge 1}\}$. Then $\bm{0}\notin Z$, and for $1\le k<l$ we must have $k\bm{t}\mod\mathcal{L}\ne l\bm{t}\mod\mathcal{L}$, otherwise $(l-k)\bm{t}\in\mathcal{L}$. Then $Z\subset \overline{\mathcal{P}(\mathcal{L})}$ is an infinite set inside a compact set, thus for all $\varepsilon>0$, there exist $1\le h<j$ such that $\|(j\bm{t}\mod\mathcal{L})-(h\bm{t}\mod\mathcal{L})\|_p<\varepsilon$. Write $j\bm{t}=\bm{v}_j+\bm{p}_j,h\bm{t}=\bm{v}_h+\bm{p}_h$ where $\bm{v}_j,\bm{v}_h\in\mathcal{L},\bm{p}_j,\bm{p}_h\in \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{L})$. Since $(j-h)\bm{t}\notin\mathcal{L}$, $0<\|(j-h)\bm{t}-(\bm{v}_j-\bm{v}_h)\|_p=\|\bm{p}_j-\bm{p}_h\|_p<\varepsilon$. This contradicts $A$ being finite. So $z\bm{t}\in\mathcal{L}$ for some $z\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}$.

Then $\mathcal{L}+\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}\bm{t}=\cup_{0\le i<z}(\mathcal{L}+i\bm{t})$ is discrete and additive, and hence it is a lattice.

label: lem:chebyshev
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:chebyshev}
Let $q$ be a prime, $\bm{h}_1,\dots,\bm{h}_G\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}_q^n\setminus\{\bm0\}$ be pairwise linearly independent, i.e.,
$\bm{h}_i\not\equiv c\bm{h}_j\pmod q$ for all $i\neq j$ and $c\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}_q$. Let $\bm{a}$ be uniform over $\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}_q^n$. Set
\[
X:=\big|\{i\in[G]:\langle\bm{h}_i,\bm{a}\rangle\equiv0\pmod q\}\big|.
\]
Then $\ensuremath{\mathbb{E}}[X]=\frac{G}{q}$ and $\operatorname*{Var}[X]= \frac{G}{q}(1-\frac1q)$. Consequently, for every $\delta>0$,
\[
\Pr[X\le(1-\delta)G/q]
\le\frac{1-1/q}{\delta^2G/q}<\frac{q}{\delta^2G}.
\]
head: environment
name: Chebyshev concentration

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $X_i:=\bm{1}\{\langle\bm{h}_i,\bm{a}\rangle\equiv0\pmod q\}$.
Then $\ensuremath{\mathbb{E}}[X_i]=\Pr[\langle\bm{h}_i,\bm{a}\rangle\equiv0\pmod q]=\frac1q$, so $\ensuremath{\mathbb{E}}[X]=G/q$. Pairwise linear independence gives $\ensuremath{\mathbb{E}}[X_iX_j]=\frac1{q^2}$ for $i\ne j$. Hence $\operatorname*{Var}[X]= \frac{G}{q}(1-\frac1q)$. The result then follows from Chebyshev's inequality.

title: Proof

label: lem: equal norm not independent
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Suppose $\bm{v}=k\bm{u}+q\bm{w}$ for some $k\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}},\bm{w}\in \mathcal{L}$. For each $a\in \{-(q-1)/2,\dots,(q-1)/2\}$, choose $b_a\in\{-(q-1)/2,\dots,(q-1)/2\}$ such that $b_a=-ak+ c_aq$ for some integer $c_a$. Set 
$$
    \bm{s}_a=\frac{a\bm{v}+b_a\bm{u}}{q}=\frac{ak\bm{u}+aq\bm{w}-ak\bm{u}+c_aq\bm{u}}{q}=a\bm{w}+c_a\bm{u}\in \mathcal{L}.
$$
But we have $\|\bm{s}_a\|_p\le \frac1q (|a|\|\bm{v}\|_p+|b_a|\|\bm{u}\|_p)=\frac{|a|+|b_a|}{q}r<r$. Now for $-(q-1)/2\le a<a'\le (q-1)/2$, if $\bm{s}_a=\bm{s}_{a'}$, this implies $a\bm{v}+b_a\bm{u}=a'\bm{v}+b_{a'}\bm{u}$. But $0<\|\bm{v}\|_p=\|\bm{u}\|_p$ and $\bm{v}\ne\pm\bm{u}$, so they are linearly independent, in contradiction to $a<a'$. This proves $\{\bm{s}_a\}_{-(q-1)/2\le a\le (q-1)/2}$ contains $q$ distinct vectors in $\mathcal{L}$ with norm less than $r$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Note that $q\mathcal{L}\subseteq \mathcal{L}' \subseteq \mathcal{L}$, so that $\mathcal{L}'$ has rank $n$ as claimed. \cref{lem:order-of-t} implies $s>1$ is well-defined, and $M:=\mathcal{L}+\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}\bm{t}$ is a lattice. Observe that $s\bm{t}' = \ensuremath{\bm{B}} (\bm{d}-s\bm{z})$, and $\langle \bm{d}-s\bm{z},\bm{a}\rangle = \langle \bm{d}-ss^*\bm{d},\bm{a}\rangle\equiv 0\pmod q$. Hence $s\bm{t}'\in\mathcal{L}'$, and $\mathcal{L}'+\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}\bm{t}'$ is also a lattice.

\paragraph{Proof of~\cref{item-one-BPT25}.} Let $A_2:=\{\bm{y}-k\bm{t}:\bm{y}\in\mathcal{L},k\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}},0<\|\bm{y}-k\bm{t}\|_p<r\}$, then $A=|A_2|+1$. For any $\bm{w}\in A_2$, write $\bm{w}=\bm{y}-k\bm{t},\ \bm{y}=\ensuremath{\bm{B}}\bm{x}$ where $\bm{x}\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}^n$. We can assume $0\le k<s$ since $s\bm{t}\in\mathcal{L}$. Note $\bm{w} = (\bm{y}-k\ensuremath{\bm{B}}\bm{z})-k\bm{t}'$. We next prove $\bm{w}\in\mathcal{L}'+\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}\bm{t}'\iff \bm{y}-k\ensuremath{\bm{B}}\bm{z}\in\mathcal{L}'$. The converse direction is trivial. Suppose $\bm{w}=\bm{y}'-e\bm{t}'$ for some $\bm{y}'\in\mathcal{L}'$, $s\bm{t}'\in\mathcal{L}'$ implies we can assume $0\le e<s$. Then we have $\bm{y}-k\ensuremath{\bm{B}}\bm{z}-\bm{y}'=(k-e)\bm{t}'=(k-e)(\bm{t}-\ensuremath{\bm{B}} \bm{z})$. Since the left hand side is in $\mathcal{L}$ and $-s<(k-e)<s$, we get $k=e$, and hence $\bm{y}-k\ensuremath{\bm{B}}\bm{z}=\bm{y}'\in\mathcal{L}'$. We have
\begin{equation}
    \bm{w}\in\mathcal{L}'+\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}\bm{t}'\iff \bm{y}-k\ensuremath{\bm{B}}\bm{z}\in\mathcal{L}'\iff \langle\bm{x}-k\bm{z},\bm{a}\rangle\equiv 0\pmod q. \label{eq:bad w condition}
\end{equation}
Recall $s\bm{t}=\ensuremath{\bm{B}}\bm{d}$, and~\cref{eq:bad w condition} is equivalent to $ \langle \bm{x}-ks^*\bm{d},\bm{a}\rangle\equiv 0\pmod q$. Since $q\nmid s$, multiplying by $s$ gives equivalence to $\langle s\bm{x}-k\bm{d},\bm{a}\rangle\equiv 0\pmod q$. 

We now prove $s\bm{x}-k\bm{d}\not\equiv0\pmod q$. Otherwise $s\bm{w}=\ensuremath{\bm{B}} (s\bm{x}-k\bm{d})\in q\mathcal{L}\subseteq qM$. Since $\bm{w}\in M$ and $q\nmid s$, we have $\bm{w}\in qM$. But $0<\|\bm{w}\|_p<r$, \cref{lem: short vec not in qL} implies $A\ge 2q-1$, contradicting the assumption that $q>A$. Therefore,
\[
\Pr[\bm{w}\in\mathcal{L}'+\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}\bm{t}']=\Pr[\langle s\bm{x}-k\bm{d},\bm{a}\rangle\equiv 0\pmod q]=\frac1q.
\]

Since $\mathcal{L}'+\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}\bm{t}'\subseteq \mathcal{L}+\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}\bm{t}$, a union bound over $\bm{w}\in A_2$ shows
\[
\Pr[\lambda_1^{(p)}(\mathcal{L}'+\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}\bm{t}')<r]\le \frac{A-1}{q}.
\]

\paragraph{Proof of~\cref{item-two-BPT25}.} Write $\{\bm{v}\in \mathcal{L}:\|\bm{v}-\bm{t}\|_p=r\}=\{\bm{v}_1,\dots,\bm{v}_G\},\ \ \bm{v}_i=\ensuremath{\bm{B}}\bm{x}_i$ for $1\le i\le G$, and define $\bm{u}_i=\bm{v}_i-\bm{t}$. Let $X :=N_p(\mathcal{L}'-\bm{t}',r)$. Note that 
\[\{ \bm{v} \in \mathcal{L}' \ : \ \|\bm{v}-\bm{t}'\|_p = r\}=(\{\bm{v}\in \mathcal{L}:\|\bm{v}-\bm{t}\|_p=r\}-\ensuremath{\bm{B}} \bm{z})\cap \mathcal{L}'
\; ,
\]so that $X \geq \sum_{i=1}^G \bm{1}\{\bm{v}_i-\ensuremath{\bm{B}}\bm{z}\in\mathcal{L}'\}$.

Define $\bm{h}_i=s\bm{x}_i-\bm{d}$, for $1\le i\le G$. We have
\begin{equation}
    \bm{v}_i-\ensuremath{\bm{B}}\bm{z}\in\mathcal{L}'\iff \langle\bm{x}_i-s^*\bm{d},\bm{a}\rangle\equiv 0\pmod q\iff \langle\bm{h}_i,\bm{a}\rangle\equiv 0\pmod q. \label{eq:condition of bi}
\end{equation}

We next show $\bm{h}_i\not\equiv 0\pmod q$. Indeed, otherwise $\ensuremath{\bm{B}}\bm{h}_i=s\bm{v}_i-s\bm{t}=s\bm{u}_i\in q\mathcal{L}\subseteq qM$. Since $\bm{u}_i\in M$ and $q\nmid s$, we have $\bm{u}_i\in qM$, and~\cref{lem: short vec not in qL} gives a contradiction.

Suppose for $i\ne j$, $\bm{h}_i\equiv k\bm{h}_j\pmod q$ for some $k\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}_q$. Then $s\bm{v}_i-s\bm{t}-ks(\bm{v}_j-\bm{t})=s(\bm{u}_i-k\bm{u}_j)\in qM$, so $\bm{u}_i-k\bm{u}_j\in qM$. So $\bm{u}_i\equiv k\bm{u}_j\pmod {qM}$, since they have equal norm $r$, \cref{lem: equal norm not independent} implies $A\ge q$ unless $\bm{u}_i=\pm\bm{u}_j$. For $i\ne j$, this happens only if $\bm{u}_i=-\bm{u}_j$, so $\bm{v}_i-\bm{t}=\bm{t}-\bm{v}_j$. Then $2\bm{t}\in\mathcal{L}$ and $s=2$.

If $s>2$, vectors $\bm{h}_1,\dots,\bm{h}_G$ are pairwise linearly independent modulo $q$. \cref{lem:chebyshev} gives 
\[
\Pr[X\le (1-\delta)G/q]< \frac{q}{\delta^2 G}.
\]
Else when $s=2$, two vectors $\bm{h}_i=-\bm{h}_j$ always survive simultaneously. We group $\bm{h}_1,\dots,\bm{h}_G$ into $G/2$ such pairs, the same lemma implies $\Pr[X\le (1-\delta)G/q]< \frac{2q}{\delta^2 G}.$

title: Remark
body_md:
We assume that $q\nmid s$ in~\cref{lem:sparsification-25} for convenience. However, we note that a different construction works if $q\mid s$. In that case, one can sample $\bm{z} \sim \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}_q^n$ and $\bm{a}$ uniformly from $\{\bm{x}\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}^n_q:\langle \bm{x},\bm{d}\rangle\equiv 0\pmod q\}$. This yields similar results for minimum distance and number of close vectors. However, in our applications (\cref{thm:large p,cor: alpha to kissing number}), $s=2$ and $q$ is a large prime. Therefore, we prove~\cref{lem:sparsification-25} only for $q\nmid s$.

Furthermore, one can also think of our choice of $\bm{a},\bm{z}$ as following~\cite[Proposition~2.5]{conf/innovations/BennettPT22}, but conditioned on $s\bm{t}'\in\mathcal{L}'$. This is equivalent to choosing a fixed $\bm{z}=s^*\bm{d}$ as in~\cref{lem:sparsification-25}.

label: lem:new-KN-to-LDL
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $S := \set{\bm{v} \in \mathcal{L} : \norm{\bm{v}}_p = \lambda_1^{(p)}(\mathcal{L})}$ be the set of the shortest non-zero vectors of $\mathcal{L}$.

We note that it suffices to prove that there exist an index-two sublattice $\mathcal{L}' \subsetneq \mathcal{L}$ of $\mathcal{L}$ and a vector $\bm{t} \in \mathcal{L} \setminus \mathcal{L}'$ such that the coset $\mathcal{L}' - \bm{t} = \mathcal{L} \setminus \mathcal{L}'$ satisfies $\card{S \cap (\mathcal{L}' - \bm{t})} > \kappa_p(\mathcal{L})/2$. 
Indeed, notice that $\card{\operatorname{CVP}_p(\bm{t}, \mathcal{L}')} = \card{S \cap (\mathcal{L}' - \bm{t})}$ as long as $S \cap (\mathcal{L}' - \bm{t})$ is non-empty. So, if $\card{S \cap (\mathcal{L}' - \bm{t})} > \kappa_p(\mathcal{L})/2$ then $(\mathcal{L}', \bm{t})$ is a $(p, n, N)$-exact locally dense lattice for $N>\kappa_p(\mathcal{L})/2$.

To that end, let $\ensuremath{\bm{B}}$ be a basis of $\mathcal{L}$ and sample $\bm{a} \sim \set{0, 1}^n \setminus \set{\bm{0}}$ uniformly at random. Let
\[
\mathcal{L}' := \set{\ensuremath{\bm{B}} \bm{x} : \bm{x} \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}^n, \inner{\bm{x}, \bm{a}} \equiv 0 \ (\mathrm{mod}\ 2)} \ \text{,}
\]
and let $\bm{t} = \ensuremath{\bm{B}} \bm{z} \in \mathcal{L} \setminus \mathcal{L}'$. (Notice that such a vector $\bm{t}$ exists since $\bm{a} \not\equiv \bm{0} \ (\mathrm{mod}\ 2)$.)

Let $\bm{v} = \ensuremath{\bm{B}}\bm{y} \in S$ and notice that $\bm{y} \not\equiv \bm{0} \ (\mathrm{mod}\ 2)$ (since otherwise $\bm{v} = \bm{0}$ or $\bm{v}/2 \in \mathcal{L}$ and $\bm{v}/2$ is shorter than $\bm{v}$). We then have that
 
   \[
    \Pr_{\bm{a}}[\bm{v} \in \mathcal{L}'-\bm{t} ] = \Pr_{\bm{a}}[\langle\bm{y},\bm{a}\rangle\equiv 1 \ (\mathrm{mod}\ 2)]> 1/2\ \text{.}
    \]
So, by linearity of expectation, $\ensuremath{\mathbb{E}}_{\bm{a}}[\ \card{S \cap (\mathcal{L}' - \bm{t})}\ ]>|S|/2=\kappa_p(\mathcal{L})/2$, hence there exists a pair $(\mathcal{L}',\bm{t})$ satisfying $\card{S \cap (\mathcal{L}' - \bm{t})} >\kappa_p(\mathcal{L})/2$, as needed.

 Observe that although the parameters we choose are not covered directly by the statement of \cite[Theorem~6.3]{wan2026nphardnesssvpeuclideanspace}, the same proof applies. Indeed, by \cite[(6.3.2)]{wan2026nphardnesssvpeuclideanspace},
\[
     |S_2(\bm{y},2k)|\cdot (2k)!>q^{(k+2)/2}\binom{2k}{2}
    \big(q^{(k-2)/2}-(2k)^{2k}\big).
\]
Moreover,
\[
    \frac{(2k)^{2k}}{q^{(k-2)/2}}=    q\left(\frac{(2k)^2}{q^{1/2}}\right)^k
    \le q\left(\frac{\alpha^2q^{1/2}}{q^{1/2}}\right)^k= q\alpha^{2k}=o(1),
\]
since $0<\alpha<1$. Hence,
\[
    q^{(k-2)/2}-(2k)^{2k}=(1-o(1))q^{(k-2)/2},
\]
and therefore $|S_2(\bm{y},2k)|\cdot (2k)!\ge(1-o(1))\binom{2k}{2}q^k$. Using $(2k)!\le (2k)^{2k}\le \alpha^{2k}q^{k/2}\le q^{k/2}$, we obtain
\[
    |S_2(\bm{y},2k)|\ge q^{k/2}=2^{\Omega(q^{1/4}\log q)}.
\]
Thus the proof of \cite[Theorem~6.3]{wan2026nphardnesssvpeuclideanspace} extends to the endpoint \(k=\Theta(q^{1/4})\).
